modelAnswer.text:
The pie chart shows how Coca-Cola's 17.1 billion unit cases were distributed by region in 2000, while the line graph traces the company's share price from 1996 to 2001.

Overall, North America was the largest regional market, while Africa and the Middle East was the smallest. The share price rose to a peak around 1998 and then fell back, ending above its starting level but below that peak.

In 2000, North America accounted for 30.4% of unit case volume, followed by Latin America at 25.7%; together the two American regions made up 56.1%, just over half the total. Europe held 20.5% and Asia 16.4%, while Africa and the Middle East contributed the remaining 7.0%.

The share price began at roughly $35–40 in 1996 and climbed, with fluctuations, to a peak of about $80 in 1998. It then declined, falling below $50 around 2000, before recovering to about $60. At the end of the period it stood at approximately $55–60, higher than at the start but well below the 1998 peak.
